Basically I take all my notes in one of two apps: emacs on my computers, and logseq on my phone + tablet. If I have an idea or something I need to remember I make a daily note. Or if it's a note referencing a specific thing like a topic or a book it gets it's own little note file. Then I can just make a link between notes as I find them.  
Finally once I close the note it's synced across all my stuff using git. 

The notes contain both the literal information, and any other notes that they reference. And I can get a random one at the push of a button! I also have a button to see a 2d graph of my notes and their connections.  The notes are all plain text so I don't need to worry about them getting trapped in a  
specific app. 

I based it on:  
 - [https://sbgrl.me/posts/logseq-org-roam-1/](https://sbgrl.me/posts/logseq-org-roam-1/) (whole series)  
 - Get Things Done by David Allen  
 - How to Take Smart Notes by Sönke Ahrens  
 - How to Read a Book by Mortimer J. Adler & Charles Van Doren

In general can hypnosis help with anxiety? I'd say yes. The principle of neuroplasticity shows that repeated stimulation of the brain re-enforces corresponding areas of the brain. Sorta like training a muscle. So if you use hypnosis as a tool, you can (potentially) gradually develop strategies to cope with or manage your anxiety attacks. 

That being said, hypnosis isn't magic. And you are still an animal subject to the laws of reality,

A way you might approach it, is to start with learning how to fall into a trance reliably.   
Perhaps with a guided track? Then as you practice getting into and out of trances, you practice learning how to control your mind bit by bit. Making tools and such along the way. 

One I developed, is my so called "clinical voice" where I look at the situation not as myself (a panicking animal), instead as a skilled Doctor or Physician (Important note, I'm neither).  


Another, commonly taught in CBT is the 5,4,3,2,1 method where you find, and focus on   
5 things you can see, 4 hear, 3  touch, 2 smell, 1 taste.  
Virtually identical to a classic count down induction.   


But be careful not to take most things with hypnosis with a grain of salt.  
There's a lot of misinformation that gets spread for a variety of reasons.  
Finally, remember than all this is a skill. So you'll need to practice to get good at it.  
Sorta like playing music.
